summary: The Wildland Firefighter Health and Safety Act establishes an interagency program, task force, research office, and new standards to improve the health, safety, and wellbeing of federal wildland firefighters.

affected_groups.effect: Receive new health and wellbeing programs, regular medical exams, exposure tracking, guaranteed paid duty time for hygiene and gear decontamination, and new respiratory protection standards.
Receive access to exposure tracking and support services when supporting fire activities outside their primary job responsibilities.
Must establish interagency task forces, specialized claims handling units, permanent research offices, reporting mechanisms, and issue new safety standards and grant programs.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Interior, Agriculture, Labor, NIOSH, OSHA)

key_provisions: Establishes an interagency Wildland Firefighter Health Task Force and a Wildland Firefighter Health Advisory Panel within the Department of the Interior.
Authorizes the Federal Wildland Firefighter Health and Wellbeing Program led by a Program Director to address occupational exposures, mental health, and cancer prevention.
Creates an Office of Firefighter Health and Safety within the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) and sets up a respiratory protection pilot program.
Directs the Department of Labor to issue interim final and permanent occupational safety and health standards for wildland firefighters through OSHA.
Establishes a special claims handling unit for fire protection activities within the Office of Workers' Compensation Programs.
Guarantees regular duty time with pay and benefits for personal hygiene, gear decontamination, and cleaning of vehicles and equipment.
Requires regular Government Accountability Office (GAO) studies and reports evaluating the progress of the Wellbeing Program.
missing_information: Exact total costs of the bill beyond specific authorized appropriations for sections 3, 4, and 5.
Specific numerical targets for respiratory protection effectiveness beyond pilot program parameters.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Wildland Firefighter Health and Safety Act establishes an interagency program, task force, research office, and new standards to improve the health, safety, and wellbeing of federal wildland firefighters.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation creates a comprehensive federal initiative spanning multiple departments to address the long-term occupational health, safety, cancer risks, and exposure concerns of federal wildland firefighters through coordinated research, standards, and worker compensation reforms.
